messages:
mike: FYI I just finished a focused sweep comparing fused-paged-v2 vs paged-fused-legacy across A100 / H100 / L40S. Observed a weird regression on H100 at seq=512, bsz=8 — fused-paged-v2 is ~18% slower than legacy. full run attached below.

bench-bot: automated results uploaded: gs://redwood-bench/attn/2026/2998877665/summary.csv :white_check_mark:

mike: paste of the key rows:``` 
GPU,model,seq,bsz,variant,median_p99_ms
A100,chat-7b,128,1,fused-paged-v2,12.3
A100,chat-7b,128,1,paged-fused-legacy,13.0
H100,chat-7b,512,8,fused-paged-v2,86.4
H100,chat-7b,512,8,paged-fused-legacy,73.2
L40S,chat-7b,1024,4,fused-paged-v2,140.1
L40S,chat-7b,1024,4,paged-fused-legacy,145.6
```

sara: hmm that's a pretty big delta at 512x8 on H100. Did you run with KV cache warm vs cold? :thinking:

mike: yes, each experiment has warm-prefill and cold-prefill variants; the numbers above are warm (KV populated). Cold shows larger variance but still similar delta.

cheng: @mike did you use the new kernel-selector heuristic from PR#5123? that changed the batchseq threshold cutoff for fusedpaged selection.

mike: yes, this run used runtime build 2026.03.12 (includes PR#5123). I also re-ran a control with kernel-selector pinned to previous heuristics and the H100 512x8 numbers matched legacy.

kim: I profiled the H100 512x8 job with nvprof and a quick CUPTI trace. Short summary: fused-paged-v2 has an extra device->host memcpy at steady-state every ~32 steps (small 64KB copies) and some kernel launch serialization that we don't see on A100. attaching flame snippet.

kim: flame snippet (truncated):```
[fused_paged_kernel] 60%\n[memcpy D->H small chunks] 12%\n[host-sync] 8%\n[other kernels] 20%\n```

mike: interesting, that memcpy pattern could be from the new eviction bookkeeping in the selector path. PR#5123 added a small async callback to query page residency.

cheng: that callback was supposed to be async and host-threaded, but might be racing into the sync path on H100 due to different stream ordering. H100 driver semantics sometimes expose ordering issues.

mike: I reproduced with `--trace-streams` enabled; I see stream 2 sync points inserted right before KV lookup on the fused path.

bench-bot: note: the regression only surfaces for bsz>=8 and seq>=384 on H100 in our sample grid. Lower bsz or A100/L40S no regression.

sara: action items?

mike: immediate mitigation: revert the residency callback in kernel-selector for H100 builds (quick patch). Longer term: make the callback fully device-only or use CUDA events instead of host sync.

cheng: I'll draft a small patch to gate the callback behind `gpu_vendor=="h100" ? skip_async_host_probe : use_probe`. also will add unit that asserts no host-syncs in hot path.

kim: I'll add a microbench that runs 512x8 on H100 with `--trace-streams` and records memcpy counters. we should add it to the perf-regress CI matrix as a post-merge check.

mike: thanks. I'll roll a canary with the revert to dedicated canary pool and re-run same sweep. posting canary run ts shortly. :thumbsup:

bench-bot: canary run queued: job 2026-03-12-2998877701. results when ready will be auto-posted.

sara: nice catch. keep notes on the diff so we don't lose the optimization idea behind the callback — it's likely valuable on A100 but harmful on H100. :eyes:

mike: logging the follow-up doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/eng-runtime/attn/kernel-selector-h100-caveats (draft)

cheng: tagging this for postmortem in eng-runtime perf board.

mike: end of thread — will update when canary completes.
